title_en: Doctors and Pharmacies (9/20): Xiao Mei Gets Glasses
note_en: 越来越 + adjective describes something changing step by step: 看黑板越来越模糊 "the board was getting blurrier and blurrier." English needs a verb like "get" or "become" plus a comparative; Chinese just puts 越来越 straight in front of the adjective, with no 很 and no word for "more."

sentences.en: He went on to explain that the strength of glasses is measured in diopters. Lenses for nearsightedness are concave, spreading the light out just enough to refocus it on the retina, while lenses for farsightedness are the opposite, convex. Because Xiao Mei's astigmatism was fairly noticeable, she would also need lenses that correct for it; otherwise, even with the right nearsighted or farsighted prescription, things would still look a little blurry or distorted.

sentences.en: He explained further that once nearsightedness has developed, the lengthening of the eyeball usually can't be reversed. Current treatments, whether ortho-k lenses, low-dose atropine drops, or multifocal lenses, can mostly only slow the progression; they can't shorten an eyeball that has already grown longer, so the earlier treatment starts, the better the results tend to be.

sentences.en: Mr. Wang mentioned that amblyopia (lazy eye) is different from nearsightedness: it happens because vision didn't finish developing properly in childhood, so even with glasses, eyesight can't be fully corrected to normal. That's why it needs treatment as early as possible once it's found; if the best age for treatment is missed, the results are much worse.
